item.title: Ja'Marr Chase explodes for 142 receiving yards in first 25 minutes of play in Madrid
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Bengals' star wide receiver is having the best first half of his career.
item.content:encoded:
Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase is having an eye-popping first half today in Madrid.

Chase caught eight passes for 142 yards and a touchdown in the first 25 minutes of play against the Falcons, helping the Bengals take a 21-10 lead over the Falcons.

It's the most receiving yards that Chase has ever had in the first half of a game in his career.

The rest of the Bengals' offense hasn't done anything special, with a total of 91 yards on any play that isn't a pass to Chase, but they haven't needed to. Chase is taking over the game.

It's going to be a long flight home from Spain for the Falcons' defense if they can't find a way to stop Chase from running free through their secondary.

item.title: Cowboys have ideal chance to end streak of allowing 20 or more points
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: It's been nearly a year since the Cowboys held an opponent under 20 points.
item.content:encoded:
It's been nearly a year since the Cowboys held an opponent under 20 points. The best chance to end that streak comes later today.

At 1:00 p.m. ET, the Cowboys visit the Colts. And the Colts have scored a total of 17 points since waving the white flag with the same-day trades of guard Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the 49ers.

Of course, they've played a couple of very good defenses, at Minnesota and at Jacksonville. Still, with the organization creating a clear impression that they've embarked on a rebuilding plan during the 2026 season — and with trade talk hovering as to running back Jonathan Taylor, quarterback Daniel Jones, and receiver Josh Downs — the Cowboys are catching the Colts at an ideal time for Dallas.

For now, the Cowboys have allowed 20 or more points for 15 straight games. It's the longest active streak in the league, and the longest streak in franchise history.

The Cowboys last held an opponent under 20 points on November 17, 2025, in a Monday night 33-16 win over the Raiders. Since then, the Cowboys have allowed 21, 28, 44, 34, 34, 23, 34, 28, 20, 34, 30, 24, 23, 21, and 33 points. That works out to an average of 28.7 points allowed per game.

Today's the day the run could end. If it doesn't, who knows when it will?

item.title: Offensive fireworks in Madrid: Joe Burrow hits Ja'Marr Chase for 47-yard touchdown
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Falcons' and Bengals' offensive stars are off to a hot start in Madrid.
item.content:encoded:
The Bengals and Falcons are putting on a show for the fans in Madrid.

In the NFL's showcase in Spain, Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow hit wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase for a 47-yard touchdown to tie the score 7-7 in the first quarter.

Both teams scored on their opening possessions, the Falcons on a seven-play, 80-yard drive and the Bengals on a five-play, 75-yard drive.

It's been an entertaining first six minutes of football at Bernabéu Stadium.

item.title: Falcons take early lead over Bengals in Madrid
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Falcons drove into the red zone on the strength of Bijan Robinson's legs, then Michael Penix threw a TD pass.
item.content:encoded:
The Falcons' offense made it look easy against the Bengals' defense on today's first drive in Madrid.

Bijan Robinson ran the ball three times for 42 yards, Michael Penix completed all three of his passes, and the Bengals committed two penalties on a seven-play, 80-yard drive that ended with a Penix one-yard touchdown pass to Charlie Woerner. It was Woerner's first career touchdown.

The extra point made it 7-0 Falcons, in a game that's a big one for both teams, who are in competitive division races.

The Bengals have struggled early in games recently, frequently falling behind in the first quarter and then coming back and winning. They're going to need to do that again.

item.title: Daniel Jones has several million reasons to want to be traded to a contender
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: A trade would be a financial win-win for Colts and Jones.
item.content:encoded:
At a time when the Colts are undoubtedly considering an exit strategy from the balance of the Daniel Jones contract, Jones has a clear incentive to be traded to a playoff contender.

The incentive comes directly from his incentive package.

Jones's two-year, $88 million deal has plenty of sweeteners for 2026. And most of them are tied to making it to the playoffs, and winning games once he gets there.

He's on track to earn up to $550,000 by racking up 90 percent offensive playing time for the season. Through eight games, he has taken 98 percent of the snaps. (Specifically, the term gives him $100,000 for 50 percent, $200,000 for 60 percent, $300,000 for 70 percent, $400,000 for 80 percent, or $550,000 for 90 percent.)

Jones also gets an extra $100,000 for each win in which he plays more than 50 percent of the snaps. To date, he has added $200,000 of a potential $800,000.

If his team wins 10 or more games and he participates in 75 percent of the offensive snaps, Jones gets another $250,000. With 75-percent playing time and a playoff berth, he gets another $250,000. With 75-percent playing time and a division title, he gets another $250,000.

Then comes the package for postseason success, with up to $2.5 million available. With 50-percent playing time and a win in the wild-card round, he gets $500,000. With 50-percent and a win in the divisional round, he gets another $500,000. With 50-percent playing time and a win in the conference championship, he gets another $500,000. With 50-percent playing time and a win in the Super Bowl, he gets another $1 million.

So, yes, Jones has plenty of reasons to want to be moved from a non-contender to a contender.

And the Colts have plenty of reasons to want to get him off the roster. He has a $10.51 million injury guarantee for 2027. At some point, the Colts could be tempted to put him in bubble wrap, like the Giants did to him in 2024.

At that point, Jones would surely repeat his request from two years ago to be released. Because, however, the trade deadline will have passed, he'd be subject to waivers.

The best outcome for the Colts (who can walk away from the Jones contract before the guarantees vest in March 2027) would be to get value for Jones now. The best outcome for Jones would be to land on a team with which he's better situated to unlock several million in incentives.

And the best destination — barring a serious injury to a contender's starting quarterback on Sunday — continues to be the Vikings.

item.title: Bill Belichick, UNC are one win away from bowl eligibility
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Former Patriots coach Bill Belichick was back in New England on Saturday, for a game between North Carolina and Connecticut.
item.content:encoded:
Former Patriots coach Bill Belichick was back in New England on Saturday, for a game between North Carolina and Connecticut.

The Tar Heels, fueled by three touchdown passes from quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. and 21 points from three Huskies turnovers, ended a two-game losing streak with a 38-21 win.

It was Belichick's first game in New England since he was fired by the Patriots after the 2023 season.

The victory moved UNC to 5-4 on the season. It puts them one win short of bowl eligibility, with three games to play.

North Carolina finishes its schedule with games against 6-3 Louisville, 4-5 Virginia, and 4-5 NC State.

Now in his second season at the college level, Belichick's overall record is 9-12.

item.title: James Pearce Jr. is active for the Falcons
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The eight-game suspension of Falcons defensive end James Pearce Jr. has ended.
item.content:encoded:
The eight-game suspension of Falcons defensive end James Pearce Jr. has ended. His second NFL season officially starts on Sunday in Madrid.

Pearce is active for the Week 9 game against the Bengals.

Pearce will play despite back tightness that made him a limited participant in Friday's practice.

The inactives for the Falcons on Sunday include quarterback Andy Dalton (emergency QB), quarterback Jack Strand, receiver Zachariah Branch, cornerback Billy Bowman Jr., cornerback Robert Longerbeam, and defensive end Drake Jackson.

Bowman, who missed the last two games with a hamstring, was considered to be healthy and ready to return.

Also out are running back Brian Robinson Jr. and defensive end Samson Ekuban. Both were placed on injured reserve recently, taking them off the 53-man roster.

A first-round pick in 2025, Pearce had 10.5 sacks as a rookie, and he finished third in the NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year voting. Felony charges filed after he repeatedly rammed his ex-girlfriend's car and resisted arrest triggered the eight-game suspension.

item.title: Lamar Jackson's message to teammates: Stay alive, and I'll be back
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Jackson is out 6-9 weeks with thumb injury.
item.content:encoded:
With plenty of discussion this week as to whether quarterback Lamar Jackson will return to the Ravens in 2027 (we think he will), the question of whether he'll be back in 2026 has been largely overlooked.

Via Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Jackson told teammates this week that he intends to return this season.

Jackson, per Rapoport, is out 6-9 weeks with a fractured and dislocated thumb.

The two-time MVP's message to the locker room was simple: "Just stay alive, and if you do I will be back."

The Ravens are currently hanging by a shrinking handful of threads. From 4-1 to 4-5, the Ravens are fading in the AFC playoff picture. But, after losses to the Browns, Bengals, Bills, and Jaguars, the schedule softens moving forward.

First up, they host the currently winless Chargers next Monday night. Then, the Ravens play at Carolina before facing the Texans.

Baltimore, which will debut Jacoby Brissett as the starting quarterback in Week 10, could be 7-5 at the bye.

After that, the stretch run won't be easy: Bucs, at Steelers, Browns, at Bengals, Steelers. Still, if Lamar could return for the Week 15 game at Pittsburgh, the Ravens could force their way back into one of the seven spots on the AFC playoff tree.

item.title: Texans are resisting trade interest in players like Jadeveon Clowney
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: It's the same story every year.
item.content:encoded:
It's the same story every year. Teams don't make final decisions as to whether they'll be buyers, sellers, or bystanders at the trade deadline until the last bit of hay is in the barn before the clock strikes 4:00 p.m. ET on the day the window closes.

As noted on Sunday morning by Mike Garafolo of NFL Network, the 2-5 Texans have received calls regarding teams that have interest in raiding the roster. The one name mentioned by Garafolo was veteran pass rusher Jadeveon Clowney.

The Texans, however, are waiting to see what happens today. A win over the Chargers in L.A. would move the Texans to 3-5. With a win in hand over the Jaguars and a rematch coming in Week 15, the Texans would still have a chance to catch Jacksonville for the AFC South crown.

A loss to the Chargers would change everything. Beyond falling to 2-6, the Texans will have lost to the lowly Chargers, this year's official Sixth Sense team that doesn't yet know it's dead.

If the Texans lose, the calls will surely intensify — and G.M. Nick Caserio will have some decisions to make.

Clowney surely would welcome the chance to land with a contender. He picked the Texans in large part because he believed they could win the Super Bowl.

item.title: Mike Vick, Norfolk State lose after his order was ignored
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Like a growing number of former NFL players, Mike Vick has become a college football coach.
item.content:encoded:
Like a growing number of former NFL players, Mike Vick has become a college football coach. Unlike many college football coaches, a direct order from Vick wasn't followed on Saturday.

It turned a likely win into a loss.

With 1:34 to play during Saturday's game between Vick's Norfolk State and North Carolina Central, Norfolk State led, 28-23. Norfolk State had the ball, facing second and five from the 50. North Carolina Central had no timeouts remaining.

While a pair of knees wouldn't have fully exhausted the remaining time, Vick told the offense to take a knee in victory formation. Two straight kneel-downs would have resulted in a punt with less than 15 seconds to play.

Instead, Norfolk State lined up in shotgun formation, the quarterback ran to the left, a defender hit him, and the quarterback fumbled.

North Carolina Central recovered at the Norfolk State 37. Five plays later, North Carolina scored a touchdown, on a 26-yard touchdown pass, making the score 29-28. (The two-point conversion attempt failed.)

Twenty-seven seconds remained. Norfolk State drove in position to attempt a game-winning field goal. The 37-yard try missed wide left.

“I don't know what happened at the end of the game," Vick told reporters after a loss that dropped Norfolk State to 4-6 on the season. "I put my headset down. I called victory formation. All we had to do was take a knee, kneel the clock out. That’s just situational football. I don’t know what happened in regards to that. I looked up and we was running the ball, and then I seen the fumble. But my final instructions was victory formation. That’s when you kneel it out. And they had, I think, zero timeouts left and the game was over practically."

"Well, I put my headset down, and I took my headset off because all we had to do was just run it three times, or two times, or kneel it out. That's called victory. I don't know what happened. A run play was called. I looked up, I seen us running the ball. I don't know what happened. I really don't. I don't know what the play call was. I don't know why we even ran that play.

“People will look at that, and that’ll go on as a teaching tape for a lot of teams across the country for years to come. I hate it had to be us. But I called victory formation. Just letting everybody know that. I called victory.”

While the strategy wouldn't have completely exhausted the clock, it was the right move. And, even if it wasn't, the coach gave the order. The order wasn't followed.

So what happened? Vick said he had taken off his headset and then later realized that a run play had been called. The fact that the offense went straight into shotgun formation suggests that it wasn't the players going rogue. Apparently, offensive coordinator Brian Sheppard decided to ignore Vick's directive.

Indeed, a somewhat chaotic postgame video (posted by Vick on Twitter) includes Vick telling his players "it was supposed to have been victory."

The video of the moments before the play in question shows the offense gathered at the numbers near the Norfolk State bench, speaking to a group of coaches who were still wearing headsets. The coach without a headset (who appears to be Vick) walked to the sideline before turning around and returning to the meeting.

It's clear that the coaches and players were having a discussion. From Vick's perspective, there was nothing to discuss.

And while Vick claims his instruction was ignored, he seemed to be a little too nonchalant at a time when he should have realized that something more detailed than telling the quarterback to line up under center, receive the snap, and take a knee was being planned.

If Vick believes Sheppard or other coaches overruled the head coach, Vick should be issuing pink slips immediately. It's possible, though, that Vick himself bears the bulk of the blame for not noticing that something other than the implementation of victory formation was coming.

item.title: Hall of Fame LB Jack Ham hospitalized after medical emergency at Penn State game
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Hall of Fame linebacker Jack Ham, who now serves as a radio analyst for Penn State football, was hospitalized in Seattle on Saturday after experiencing a medical emergency.
item.content:encoded:
Hall of Fame linebacker Jack Ham, who now serves as a radio analyst for Penn State football, was hospitalized in Seattle on Saturday after experiencing a medical emergency.

Penn State coach Matt Campbell said after the 28-25 win over Washington that Ham was assisted by play-by-play announcer Steve Jones.

"If it's not for Steve, what he did, I don’t know if we have as good a news as we do right now," Campbell said, via Adam Rittenberg of ESPN. Campbell added that Jones's efforts to save Ham were "heroic."

Ham is in stable condition.

Ham, 77, has served as the Penn State radio analyst since 2000. He won four Super Bowls, made eight straight Pro Bowls, and was named first-team All-Pro six consecutive times in a 12-year career with the Steelers.

Ham was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1988, after retiring from football in 1982.

item.title: Deion Sanders says Colorado deserves better after falling to 3-6
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Colorado lost again on Saturday night, and afterward head coach Deion Sanders said he knows his team isn't good enough.
item.content:encoded:
Colorado lost again on Saturday night, and afterward head coach Deion Sanders said he knows his team isn't good enough.

Saturday's 20-10 loss to Arizona State dropped Colorado to 3-6 this season, and dropped Sanders to 19-27 in four years as Colorado's head coach.

"The season doesn't look good," Sanders said afterward. "It doesn't look good. I'm not crazy. I can see clearly. You think I'm happy? I'm not happy with the outcomes. I'm not a loser by any means, and I hate the fact that we're coming up on the short end of these games."

Sanders said he feels for Colorado fans and players because he doesn't think he has done enough to put them in a position to win.

"It's not a personal hurt for me, I hurt because you guys deserve better and the team deserves better. We should win. We should put our best foot forward. And I'm not seeing that," Sanders said.

Sanders ran through the stats from the game and then said his team hadn't played well enough.

"The fan base deserves better. They really do," Sanders said.

Ultimately, Sanders says, it's on him to coach better.

"We've just got to do better," Sanders said. "And that starts with me."

item.title: Report: Colts have told teams they were offered a fourth-round pick for Josh Downs
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: A third-round pick appears to be what the Colts are trying to get to trade Downs.
item.content:encoded:
The Colts are putting out word to the rest of the league that if you want to trade for wide receiver Josh Downs, you'll need to beat an offer of a fourth-round pick.

Indianapolis has told other teams that it received an offer of a fourth for Downs, according to ESPN.

Downs has asked the Colts to trade him, and the Colts would seem likely to be willing to grant that request, given that he's in the final year of his rookie contract and they have already traded Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner and have had trade talks about other players.

Downs was a third-round pick in 2023 and leads the Colts with 330 receiving yards this season.

The Colts could also try to trade wide receiver Keenan Allen, who's second on the team with 325 receiving yards this season, as they attempt to move on from a miserable 2026 season and start to focus on building for 2027 and beyond.

item.title: Cam Jordan will become third defensive player to play 250 games with same team
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: When the Saints host the Browns on Sunday, New Orleans defensive end Cam Jordan will reach a rare milestone.
item.content:encoded:
When the Saints host the Browns on Sunday, New Orleans defensive end Cam Jordan will reach a rare milestone.

The Week 9 game will be Jordan's 250th. Via NBC Sports research, Jordan will become only the third defensive player in NFL history to play 250 or more games with the same team.

The others are Darrell Green, who played 295 games for Washington from 1983 through 2002, and Jim Marshall, who played 270 games for the Vikings from 1961 through 1979.

Jordan, the son of former Vikings tight end Steve Jordan, was a first-round pick in 2011. His dad played in 176 games from 1982 through 1994.

Cam is an eight-time Pro Bowler, with 132.0 career sacks. He's currently 22nd on the all-time list.

item.title: Player Personnel Handbook implies that the NFL can delay (or deny) Brandon Aiyuk's reinstatement
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The CBA is silent on the issue.
item.content:encoded:
Until very recently, people throughout the league believed that the procedure for returning from the reserve/left squad list was administrative, and essentially automatic.

The Brandon Aiyuk case shows that, in the NFL's view, it definitely is not.

The Collective Bargaining Agreement is silent on the topic of the reserve/left squad list. The relevant language regarding placement (and eventual reinstatement) from the reserve/left squad list appears in the NFL's Player Personnel Handbook.

In the year when the player is placed on reserve/left squad, he can't play for his current team or any other team. His season is basically over. The window for reinstatement opens the next year.

Here's the key language from the Player Personnel Handbook regarding reinstatement: "A player on Reserve/Left Squad must apply to the Commissioner for reinstatement to his club's Active List. No player on Reserve/Left Squad shall be reinstated in the same season in which he is placed on Reserve. A player applying for reinstatement in a season subsequent to the season in which he is placed on Reserve/Left Squad is prohibited from being reinstated in the last 30 days of the regular season or thereafter during the postseason, and no such player will be reinstated during the period between the trading deadline of a subsequent season and the 30-day deadline unless the club initiates the reinstatement request and the Commissioner approves it."

While the provision doesn't say it expressly, the language implies that the Commissioner has apparently unlimited discretion when it comes to approving the application to reinstate the player. In Aiyuk's case, the Commissioner has dragged his feet since October 27, setting the stage for an apparent effort by the 49ers to leverage Aiyuk's desire to be reinstated to his willingness to reimburse up to $13 million in previously-paid bonus money.

The NFL Players Association has remained silent throughout the process, and perhaps for good reason. The absence of any provision in the CBA regarding the mechanics of the reserve/left squad list arguably means that the situation falls within the NFL's "management rights" clause, which allows the various teams "to manage and direct their operations in any manner whatsoever, except as specifically limited by the provisions of this Agreement."

With no limitations in the CBA as to the operation of the reserve/left squad list (or reinstatement from it), the NFLPA may be without options.

Precedent becomes relevant to the overall analysis. How has the league handled past requests for reinstatement from the reserve/left squad list? If the league has previously not delayed reinstatement (for whatever reason), there's an argument to be made that it should not be delayed as to Aiyuk.

Regardless, it's becoming increasingly obvious that the NFL and the 49ers are working together to tie Aiyuk's reinstatement to his satisfaction of the debt that the 49ers believe Aiyuk has incurred through his prior default under his contract. It should be two separate issues, with the 49ers having the ability to pursue the recovery of bonus money from Aiyuk and Aiyuk having the ability to be reinstated. By tying the two together, the 49ers have found a way to condition Aiyuk's reinstatement on his willingness to wire a significant payment to the 49ers.

Can the NFL and the 49ers do that? For now, they are. The question is whether Aiyuk and/or the NFLPA can come up with a legal argument against the obvious effort to block Aiyuk's return until he returns millions to the 49ers.

If Aiyuk wants to be reinstated quickly, his best (and perhaps only) play will be to return millions to the 49ers, with the ensuing goal of earning it back as his career continues elsewhere.

item.title: In defending his willingness to spend, Jerry Jones may have admitted to tampering
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: On Friday, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones tried to reverse the perception/reality that he deliberately underspends on coaches.
item.content:encoded:
On Friday, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones tried to reverse the perception/reality that he deliberately underspends on coaches. His explanation regarding the willingness to spend included an important admission.

"I have been trying to lure very successful coaches away from the teams they were on," Jones said on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas.

Unless he was referring to college coaches (or high-school coaches), that's tampering. Period. End of discussion.

It could be false — an effort to bolster the idea that, yes, he's willing to spend. Still, the effort to put out the frugality fire he started on Tuesday by ridiculously claiming there’s no correlation between coaching pay and winning included a nonchalant concession that he has tried to pry NFL coaches away from their current teams, in blatant violation of the rules.

Will the NFL look into this one? Probably not. Because the league office surely realizes, as the rest of us do, that Jerry was simply saying whatever he had to say to lessen the impact of the accidental truth he told on Tuesday regarding a deliberate reluctance to do whatever he needs to do to make his team as good as it can be.

item.title: Report: Colts are in trade talks regarding QB Daniel Jones
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The list of "multiple teams" currently includes the Ravens (who pivoted elsewhere) and the Vikings.
item.content:encoded:
The Indianapolis fire sale could indeed extend to the man who was supposed to become a franchise quarterback there.

According to ESPNFL, the Colts have engaged in trade talks this week regarding Daniel Jones, speaking to "multiple teams."

The precise language of the report identifies only one team as actually talking to the Colts. From the article, the Ravens "were one team to check in on Jones." The Ravens ultimately struck a deal with the Cardinals for quarterback Jacoby Brissett, whose plunge from No. 1 to No. 3 on the depth chart made it clear to the rest of the league that he was available.

The only other team mentioned by name is the Vikings, and the report points only to "[s]peculation" involving Minnesota. (We've been “speculating” about it since the immediate aftermath of Sunday's loss by the Vikings in Detroit.)

Past ESPNFL reporting on a potential trade for running back Jonathan Taylor ultimately listed five teams as talking to the Colts (Giants, Seahawks, Broncos, Packers, Vikings). The fact that other teams weren't mentioned as to Jones suggests that, frankly, there may not be other teams.

Really, which current contender would want him? The Vikings are the only potential playoff team that checks the box as possibly needing a starter right now. And only the Vikings and Giants are contenders with which Jones has direct experience. (The Giants wouldn't want a Jones reunion, and Jones surely wouldn't want it, either.)

That could change this weekend, obviously. One injury to a starter could alter the dynamics, spurring another contender to pick up the phone and make a push for Jones. The most memorable example of that came 15 years ago, when a broken collarbone to Raiders quarterback Jason Campbell prompted a quick deal for Bengals quarterback Carson Palmer, who had decided he didn't want to play for the team that had drafted him — and who had yet to report.

Three years ago, Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins popped an Achilles tendon two days before the deadline, forcing the Vikings to scramble at the deadline to do a deal with the Cardinals for quarterback Josh Dobbs.

Absent a multi-week injury to a starting quarterback on a contender that doesn't believe its backup can hold down the fort, the Vikings may be the only team that wants Jones at the deadline.

The preferences of Daniel Jones become a factor, too. If (as we firmly believe) he's not happy that the Colts folded the tents by trading guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner after a 2-5 start that included an overtime loss to the Chiefs and a toe-to-toe battle with the then-unbeaten Vikings, Jones would have a clear interest in hopping to a contender.

The Vikings wanted to keep Jones after the 2024 season. He opted to sign with the Colts in part because he saw a more realistic path to winning the job over 2023 first-rounder Anthony Richardson in Indianapolis than 2024 first-rounder J.J. McCarthy in Minneapolis. If he's told that a return to Minnesota would include being installed immediately as QB1, he'd surely prefer that to a lost season with the Colts.

Andd Jones has power over this process. Beyond the basic reality that no team wants a starting quarterback who doesn't want to play for it, the 2027 roster bonus and base salary that become fully guaranteed in March ($10.51 million) are currently guaranteed for injury. The ESPNFL article mentions that Jones could waive the injury guarantee in order to expedite a deal.

The reverse of that (Jones refusing to waive the injury guarantee) means that Jones could block a trade, if avoiding a potential eight-figure guarantee for 2027 is a dealbreaker for his prospective employer.

Our guess? Right now, only the Vikings currently have interest in Jones. And a trade for Jones becomes a very viable possibility if the Vikings lose to the Bills on Monday with Carson Wentz playing quarterback.

Given the possibility that another team will emerge as a competitor to get Jones, it's also possible that the Vikings have already decided to trade for Jones after Monday night's game — win or lose — and that the two teams have agreed to keep it under wraps until Week 9 ends.

Either way, if the oft-injured Jones plays on Sunday against the Cowboys and gets injured, that would kill any chance to trade him. That makes it important to monitor Sunday's game carefully. If the Colts apply a quick hook to Jones, it could mean that he's already gone.

Lawrence injured his ankle in Sunday's loss to the Cardinals, and coach Brian Schottenheimer had announced the rookie would miss multiple weeks.

Lawrence will miss at least four games on IR.

The first-round pick has 13 tackles, a sack and three quarterback hits, while playing 41 percent of the defensive snaps.

In a corresponding move, the Cowboys activated outside linebacker Marist Liufau from injured reserve. Liufau broke his forearm in the preseason finale. He returned to practice Oct. 22.

Cowboys defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard, who is in his 21-day return-to-practice window, will remain on injured reserve. He has a calf injury but had full practices all week.

The Cowboys also announced they elevated wide receiver Jordan Hudson and tight end James Mitchell from the practice squad.

Tight ends Jake Ferguson and Luke Schoonmaker are questionable to play, and at wide receiver, KaVontae Turpin is out and George Pickens is questionable.

item.title: Rams listed Matthew Stafford with elbow injury because reporters asked about ice on it
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: On Monday, reporters asked Rams coach Sean McVay about quarterback Matthew Stafford having ice on his throwing arm after Sunday's win over the Chargers.
item.content:encoded:
On Monday, reporters asked Rams coach Sean McVay about quarterback Matthew Stafford having ice on his throwing arm after Sunday's win over the Chargers. On Wednesday, the Rams listed Stafford as having an elbow injury.

Yes, there's a connection.

“Really, it's because you guys asked me about it earlier in the week," McVay told reporters on Friday regarding the decision to disclose an elbow injury for Stafford. "It's more semantical than anything else. It's normal, like what he told you guys, but because you guys asked me about him having ice on his elbow. . . . He's been full, hasn't missed any sort of reps so normal management stuff that he's been doing over the last few years.”

It conjures memories of the Patriots' one-time habit of listing former quarterback Tom Brady as "probable" with a "right shoulder" injury. That all started because he had ice on his shoulder in the locker room, reporters inquired, and the team decided to just put him on the injury report every week.

Has the elbow situation affected Stafford's throwing?

“I haven't seen any of that," McVay said. "I told you guys he'd be better equipped to talk about it. He's been a full participant, been awesome. He's spinning the ball. He's been able to activate all parts of the field with great timing, rhythm, and accuracy so he's been great.”

So either he has an actual elbow injury that the Rams had been concealing, or he doesn't really have an elbow injury but they listed him as having one because reporters noticed ice on his arm and asked McVay about it. Neither explanation seems to reflect the true spirit of the injury report, which expects real injuries — and only real injuries — to be disclosed.

Either Stafford has an elbow injury that was previously hidden or he doesn't have an elbow injury and the claim that he has one is a middle finger to the meddling reporters who were doing their jobs. Neither explanation is a preferred alternative to the unvarnished truth.

item.title: Myles Garrett: Rams' opponents will have to pick their poison, me or Aaron Donald
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Garrett and Donald will play together for the first time on Sunday against the Commanders.
item.content:encoded:
Rams defensive end Myles Garret and defensive tackle Aaron Donald will finally be on the field together Sunday in Washington, and Garrett says that's going to be bad news for opposing offenses for the rest of the season.

Donald did not play in Week 1 because he was still ramping up for the season after returning from his two-year retirement, and Garret hasn't played since Week 1 because of knee surgery. Garrett said the two of them together, two multiple-time Defensive Player of the Year award winners side by side, will present a unique challenge for opposing offenses.

"I think offenses really have to pick their poison. Who's going to be freed up this play? I think either of us are pretty good at winning one-on-one, so we'll have some fun," Garrett said. "Going into this season I never thought I'd have the chance, and as you all know he kept us in suspense for quite a while, so it was very exciting, and I'm looking forward to getting on the field and playing some real snaps with him."

Garrett said his poor performance in Week 1 against the 49ers showed him he needed knee surgery, something he would have preferred to avoid.

"I was frustrated after the game. I knew that wasn't me, and I was being hampered by something," Garrett said. "I didn't want to miss any time, but I had to be realistic about where I was physically, and I had to make the best choice for me and the team."

But now Garrett is back, and he said he and Donald playing together can give the Rams an "elite defense" for the rest of the season.

item.title: Nick Sirianni admits that he misled reporters about quarterback situation
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Instead of covering up one lie with another lie, Sirianni opted to tell the truth that he hadn't.
item.content:encoded:
How do you know when a football coach is lying? If he's good at it, you don't.

Because they all do. Particularly in so-called "must-lie" situations.

There's an art to it. A way to conceal a lie with another lie. On Friday, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni opted not to lie about the fact that he lied on Monday when he told reporters that quarterback Tanner McKee would not be benched.

"Tanner’s our guy," Sirianni said. "We're not making any changes there."

On Wednesday, the Eagles made a change there, elevating Joe Milton over McKee. The move was announced after Sirianni had his midweek media availability, which prevented him from being asked questions about the change in position from "Tanner's our guy" to "Tanner's not our guy."

On Friday, Sirianni finally faced the music regarding his comments from Monday. In lieu of coming up with an explanation premised on the idea that what he said was true when he said it and circumstances changed, Sirianni surprisingly admitted that he wasn't telling the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth to reporters and, in turn, the fans.

"I was going to hold onto that as long as I possibly could, every second, every minute," Sirianni said. "Again, I'm not real shy with you guys. I'm going to tell you what I want to tell you guys. I respect the job that y'all have to do, but I'm going to tell you what I want to tell you guys because I'm always going to protect the team first and foremost.

"Every second that goes by in a situation like that, that you can hold onto information as long as you possibly can, is a little less time for the opponent to get ready for the game. I know there's a lot of interest in everything that you all want to hear, the fans want to hear. My job is to win football games, do everything we can do to help win football games, protect the guys here on this football team, and handle everything that I can inside."

In an industry where the truth is only told when it's coincidental to strategic interests, it's jarring that Sirianni told the truth that he was lying. It would have been easy to say, "We took a more careful look at the situation after Monday." Or, even more simply, "We changed our mind. Shit happens."

Instead, Sirianni opted to say, essentially, "Bullshit happens." Instead of bothering to concoct a cover story regarding his lie, he said, essentially, "Yeah. I lied. I'll do it whenever I feel like I have to."

That's the most important thing to remember. Coaches lie whenever they feel like they have to. Despite that fact, reporters and fans routinely take their words at face value, swallowing the bullshit while saying, "Thank you, sir, may I have another?"

So thank you, Nick, for making my job a little easier. In my first week of law school, one of the professors said, "The most important thing I can do for you is to give you a good crap filter."

Because crap is everywhere. Usually, the people spewing it don't admit it. When they do, it provides a tangible reminder as to whatever they say in the future.

For Sirianni, that's the most problematic aspect of his decision to tell the truth about lying. There's now an "Exhibit A" to which anyone and everyone can point as to anything and everything he says when assessing whether he's being straight with reporters and, in turn, with fans.

item.title: Philip Rivers completes high-school season, confirms interview with NC State
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: It's looking more and more like former NFL and NC State quarterback Philip Rivers will be the next coach of the Wolfpack.
item.content:encoded:
It's looking more and more like former NFL and NC State quarterback Philip Rivers will be the next coach of the Wolfpack.

Brian Murphy of WRAL has posted video of Rivers's comments from last night, after the high-school team he coaches exited the playoffs in Alabama.

Rivers confirmed that he recently interviewed for the job, which became open two weeks ago when Dan Doeren was fired in his 14th season at NC State. Rivers immediately became a candidate. By last weekend, Rivers reportedly emerged as the focus.

Since then, the Wolfpack also interviewed former NFL and NC State quarterback Russell Wilson.

"We'll see what the future holds," Rivers said, adding that he plans to "take it one day at a time."

If he goes, it will end his tenure at St. Michael Catholic High School in Fairhope, Alabama. He became the head coach in 2021.

"We didn't have a stadium a few years ago," Rivers said, turning emotional. "If it were to be the last time out here, shoot, a lot was accomplished."

If it was the last time for Rivers at St. Michael, it means there will be a first time for him never year at NC State.

item.title: Broncos and Bo Nix have won 16 straight one-score games
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Broncos keep finding ways to win games — especially close games.
item.content:encoded:
The Broncos keep finding ways to win games — especially close games.

Denver has won 16 straight games decided by one score or less. Quarterback Bo Nix has been the starter in each of the games.

Via NBC Sports research, the streak ties the 2023-24 Chiefs (with starting quarterback Patrick Mahomes) for the longest streak since 1950.

The Broncos last lost a one-score game in Week 3 of the 2025 season, 23-20 at the Chargers. Since then, the Broncos have won every one-score game in which they have played.

This year, they're doing it despite being routinely outgained. For the season, they have a yardage differential of minus-658 — third worst in the NFL. And the Broncos have won three games in 2026 despite being outgained by 100 or more yards.

The record for any season is four wins, accomplished by eight different teams. With two more this year, the Broncos will have the record to themselves.

The next opportunity to win a one-score game comes on Sunday, at the Panthers in a rematch of Super Bowl 50.

item.title: Vikings could end up with both Daniel Jones and Jonathan Taylor
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: With Minnesota linked to both players, why not do a package deal?
item.content:encoded:
Before Week 8, the Vikings had been linked to Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. After Week 8, Colts quarterback Daniel Jones became a potentially more attractive target for the Vikings.

With the trade deadline less than three days away, why not both?

The performance of quarterback Kyler Murray in the 19-15 loss to the Lions made the passing game a front-burner issue for the Vikings. But the running game remains not good enough.

In Detroit, running back Jordan Mason had eight carries for 20 yards. Running back Aaron Jones had five carries for 22 yards.

A package deal could allow the Colts to get the first-round pick they won't get by trading Taylor alone. And perhaps the Colts could get another pick or two, perhaps contingent on the playing time and/or performance of either or both players.

Regardless, with Minnesota previously linked to Taylor and currently linked to Jones, the Colts trading both to the same team could get Indianapolis something they won't get by trading Taylor and Jones to two different teams — a first-round pick.

item.title: Mason McCormick wasn't fined for dumping Jared Verse on his head
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Browns defensive end Jared Verse is getting upset.
item.content:encoded:
Browns defensive end Jared Verse is getting upset.

Well, even more upset.

Verse, who was miffed at being dumped on his head by Steelers guard Mason McCormick on an extra-point try last Sunday — and at his teammates for not rushing to his defense, will surely be unhappy to learn that the NFL didn't fine McCormick for his WWE move.

McCormick was flagged for unnecessary roughness on the play.

It's unclear why the league didn't fine McCormick. The league never explains the basis for not imposing a financial penalty on a given player.

Regardless, the league was as unbothered by the play as the other Browns players were. And it's likely that Verse will have something to say about it after Sunday's game at the Saints.
